gloss: all for nothing; a waste; come to nothing

definitions.gloss: all for nothing; a waste; come to nothing; futile
definitions.explanation: An idiomatic expression meaning that effort, time, or investment has been wasted and come to nothing, like bubbles on water that quickly disappear.

examples.japanese: {努力|どりょく}が{水|みず}の{泡|あわ}になった。
examples.english: All my effort was for nothing.

examples.japanese: ここで{諦|あきら}めたら{今|いま}までの{苦労|くろう}が{水|みず}の{泡|あわ}だ。
examples.english: If I give up now, all my hard work will have been for nothing.

examples.japanese: {一|ひと}つのミスで{三年間|さんねんかん}の{準備|じゅんび}が{水|みず}の{泡|あわ}になってしまった。
examples.english: A single mistake caused three years of preparation to go down the drain.

notes:
A vivid metaphor comparing wasted effort to bubbles on water — they appear briefly and then vanish without a trace. Almost always used in the pattern ～が{水|みず}の{泡|あわ}になる (to come to nothing) or ～が{水|みず}の{泡|あわ}だ (is all for nothing). The expression emphasizes not just failure but the transience and complete loss of what was invested.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {努力|どりょく}が{水|みず}の{泡|あわ}になる: efforts come to nothing
- {苦労|くろう}が{水|みず}の{泡|あわ}だ: hardship was all for nothing
- ～が{水|みず}の{泡|あわ}と{消|き}える: to vanish like bubbles on water

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {台無|だいな}しにする: to ruin; to spoil — focuses on someone actively ruining something, while {水|みず}の{泡|あわ} emphasizes the result of loss
- {徒労|とろう}に{終|お}わる: to end in vain — more formal; used in written language
- {無駄|むだ}になる: to become wasted — the most straightforward way to say something was pointless
- {元|もと}も{子|こ}もない: to lose everything, including the original investment — emphasizes total loss
